backlog.spec: Compute grouped-CV out-of-fold Tanimoto GP predictions on the training set as one extra feature for the descriptor LightGBM. For test molecules use the full-train GP prediction as that feature. Then use the LightGBM output alone blended with the GP at the existing weights.
backlog.title: LightGBM on descriptors plus GP OOF prediction feature

backlog.spec: fit_predict in train.py currently transforms the target to uniform ranks with y = rankdata(train_y) / len(train_y) before fitting both the descriptor LightGBM and the Tanimoto GP. A uniform target has hard edges and heavy mass at the extremes, which is awkward for the squared-loss GP in particular. Replace it with the normal-score (van der Waerden) transform: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)), which maps the ranks to a standard-normal shape. Nothing else changes: the GP prior mean subtraction, choose_sigma2, the LightGBM fit and the final rank blend all work unchanged since the transform is strictly monotone and the output is rank-averaged anyway. This is a one-line change plus the norm import.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform

backlog.spec: Add a helper std_smiles(s) that parses the SMILES with RDKit, keeps the largest fragment via rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, neutralizes charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and returns Chem.MolToSmiles of the result, falling back to the original string if parsing fails. Apply it to train_smiles and test_smiles at the top of fit_predict, so that desc_features, bit_fingerprints and MurckoScaffold all see the standardized molecules. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same.
backlog.title: Parent-fragment standardization before featurization

backlog.spec: The descriptor branch of train.py is a LightGBM regressor with the default L2 objective, fitted on the uniform rank target y = rankdata(train_y) / n. Since only the Spearman correlation of the output matters and the rank target is bounded in (0, 1], squared loss spends capacity on the extreme ranks. Change the LightGBM to objective='huber' with alpha=0.1 (about one tenth of the target range), keeping all other hyperparameters (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) and the whole GP branch and 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. This is a two-argument edit; if huber is clearly worse the same slot tells us the loss shape is not the bottleneck.
backlog.title: Huber objective for the descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Each of the 15 harness fits currently trains one LightGBM on descriptors with random_state=seed, and the GP is deterministic. Reduce prediction variance by averaging the descriptor model over 5 seeds: fit lgb.LGBMRegressor with identical hyperparameters but random_state = seed + k for k in range(5) (subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.5 make each fit genuinely different), rank-normalize each model's test prediction, and average the five rank vectors to form p_desc. Also drop n_estimators to 300 if the runtime grows uncomfortable; the current single-model job is fast (well under the 10-minute cap for 15 fits), so 5 fits should still fit. Keep the GP branch and the 0.6/0.4 final rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged models for variance reduction

backlog.spec: In train.py the Tanimoto-kernel GP uses Morgan bit fingerprints with RADIUS=2 and N_BITS=2048 (see bit_fingerprints). Replace this single fingerprint with an inner-CV choice over a small grid of fingerprint settings: (radius, fpSize) in {(2,2048), (3,2048), (3,4096), (2,1024)}. Generalize bit_fingerprints to take radius and fpSize arguments, and inside fit_predict compute the training Tanimoto kernel for each setting, score it with the same scaffold-grouped 5-fold GroupKFold Spearman loop already used in choose_sigma2 (reuse that code path, with sigma2 fixed at 0.3 during the fingerprint search), then keep the best setting and run the existing choose_sigma2 plus gp_mean on it. Keep the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM unchanged. Cache fingerprints per (smiles, radius, fpSize) in a module-level dict so the 15 fits stay inside the 10-minute budget.
backlog.title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP

backlog.spec: train.py blends a descriptor LightGBM (weight 0.6) with a Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP (weight 0.4). Add a third member that reuses the same GP machinery but a structurally different fingerprint: hashed atom-pair bits (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048)) concatenated with topological-torsion bits (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048)) into one 4096-bit binary vector. Build its Tanimoto kernel with the existing tanimoto function, reuse choose_sigma2 and gp_mean exactly as for the Morgan GP, and make the final prediction the rank average with weights 0.5 for the descriptor LightGBM, 0.25 for the Morgan GP and 0.25 for the new atom-pair/torsion GP (fixed weights, no search). Atom pairs and torsions encode topological distance rather than local environments, so the new member should decorrelate from the Morgan GP.
backlog.title: Third blend member: atom-pair plus torsion Tanimoto GP

backlog.spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM five times inside fit_predict, using seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4. Each fit keeps all other settings the same, with colsample_bytree=0.5 and subsample=0.8. Average the five test predictions before ranking. This stabilises the descriptor member, which is the noisiest part of the blend, and uses only the seed argument.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged, feature-bagged descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: train.py currently builds the GP kernel from a single Morgan bit fingerprint with RADIUS = 2 and N_BITS = 2048 (see bit_fingerprints and the module-level settings). These two numbers were never tuned. Make bit_fingerprints take radius and fpSize as arguments, then run one job per configuration is not possible, so instead average over fingerprint scales: build three bit fingerprint matrices, (radius 1, 2048 bits), (radius 2, 2048 bits) and (radius 3, 4096 bits), compute a Tanimoto kernel for each, and for each kernel run the existing choose_sigma2 plus gp_mean pipeline. Rank-transform the three test prediction vectors (rankdata / n) and average them with equal weight to form p_fp. Keep the descriptor LightGBM branch and the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. If runtime becomes a concern, call choose_sigma2 only on the radius-2 kernel and reuse that sigma2 for the other two.
backlog.title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP

backlog.spec: Build a kernel K = Tanimoto(Morgan bits) * exp(-gamma * ||z_i - z_j||^2/d) where z are the quantile-clipped, standardized RDKit descriptors of the top 30 by LightGBM importance (or all, clipped to ±5), gamma=0.5. Use it in the GP in place of the pure Tanimoto kernel. Keep the sigma2 selection.
backlog.title: Product kernel Tanimoto times descriptor RBF

backlog.spec: fit_predict currently maps the target to uniform ranks with y = rankdata(train_y)/len(train_y). Replace this with a Gaussian-rank (normal score) transform: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)). This leaves the ordering identical but spreads the tails, which changes what the squared-error objectives of both the descriptor LightGBM and the Tanimoto GP optimize (the GP prior mean subtraction in gp_mean also becomes better centred). Change nothing else: both models still see the same y, and the final output stays the 0.6/0.4 rank average of the two model predictions, so the transform only affects fitting, not the reported scale.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank (normal score) target transform

backlog.spec: Replace the parallel rank blend with a sequential (boosted) composition. First fit the descriptor LightGBM on the rank target y exactly as now and obtain its out-of-fold training predictions using scaffold-grouped 5-fold GroupKFold (groups from MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, as in choose_sigma2) so the residuals are honest. Then fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (same bit_fingerprints, tanimoto, choose_sigma2, gp_mean) to the residual r = y - oof_pred instead of to y. The final prediction is the full-data LightGBM test prediction plus the GP residual prediction, returned as ranks divided by n. This lets the fingerprint model model only what the descriptors miss, instead of competing with them under a fixed 0.6/0.4 weight. Keep W_DESC unused or remove it.
backlog.title: Residual Tanimoto GP on top of the descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: The GP kernel in train.py is a plain Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity. Multiply it by a smooth descriptor kernel so that molecules must be similar both structurally and in physicochemical space. Build Z from a small, stable descriptor subset (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHAcceptors, NumHDonors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, RingCount), standardize it with the training mean and sd, clip to [-5, 5], and form R = exp(-gamma * squared euclidean distance / d) with gamma chosen from {0.25, 1.0} by the same scaffold-grouped CV Spearman loop already used in choose_sigma2. The GP kernel becomes K = K_tanimoto * (0.5 + 0.5 * R) (so the descriptor term modulates rather than dominates). Keep choose_sigma2, gp_mean and the 0.6/0.4 final rank blend otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Product kernel of Tanimoto and descriptor RBF for the GP

backlog.spec: Set objective='huber' with alpha=0.2 in the LGBMRegressor, since the rank target lies in [0,1]. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Huber objective for descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Instead of selecting a single sigma2, average the GP predictions from sigma2 in (0.1,0.3,1.0) with equal weights, removing the CV selection (faster, less noisy). Then rank-blend as before.
backlog.title: Sigma2 ensemble of GP posteriors

backlog.spec: choose_sigma2 currently picks a single noise level from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by scaffold-grouped CV Spearman and that one value is used in gp_mean. Selecting on ~970 molecules with a noisy criterion is unstable, so instead delete the selection and average: compute p_fp as the mean of the rank-normalized GP posterior means over the whole grid, i.e. for each s2 in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} call gp_mean(K_tr, y, K_te, s2), convert each prediction vector to ranks divided by n, and average the four rank vectors. This is a cheap Bayesian-model-average over the noise hyperparameter: it needs one extra linear solve per s2 and removes an inner CV loop, so the job gets faster. Keep choose_sigma2 removed (or unused) and keep the final 0.6/0.4 blend with the descriptor LightGBM unchanged.
backlog.title: Average GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of selecting one

backlog.spec: W_DESC = 0.6 in train.py was chosen when the fingerprint member was an ExtraTrees model; the member has since been replaced by the stronger Tanimoto-kernel GP, so the fixed weight is likely stale. Make a one-line change setting W_DESC = 0.45, i.e. the descriptor LightGBM rank gets 0.45 and the GP rank gets 0.55. Change nothing else. This is deliberately a single-constant probe (no inner search, which has already been tried and cost accuracy); if it moves the loss by more than the ~0.007 noise sd it identifies the direction the weight should go, and if not the simple 0.6 stays.
backlog.title: Shift the blend weight toward the fingerprint GP

backlog.spec: train.py fits one global Tanimoto-kernel GP on all ~780 training molecules per fold. Hepatocyte clearance structure-activity relationships are local, so add a local variant and average it in. For each test molecule, find its 150 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (using the Morgan bit fingerprints already computed by bit_fingerprints and the tanimoto helper), solve the GP on that submatrix only (reuse gp_mean with the same sigma2 that choose_sigma2 returns for the global kernel) and take the posterior mean at that single test point. This costs about 780 small 150x150 solves per fold, which is fast with numpy. Rank-transform both the global and the local posterior means and average them 50/50 to form p_fp; keep the final 0.6/0.4 blend against the descriptor LightGBM unchanged.
backlog.title: Local GP on the k most similar training molecules

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, build a second hashed fingerprint per molecule with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and, separately, GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048), using GetFingerprintAsNumPy as bit vectors. Keep the existing Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP as the fingerprint member but replace its kernel with the Tanimoto kernel of the atom-pair bits, leaving choose_sigma2, gp_mean and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. Only the kernel input changes. Do not add a new model.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprint Tanimoto GP

memo: Helped: moving from the RF baseline (about 0.6103) to a rank-averaged blend of descriptor LightGBM plus a fingerprint model (0.5337), then rank-transforming the target (0.5123), then swapping ExtraTrees for a Tanimoto-kernel GP on Morgan bits (0.4971/0.4965; incumbent, mean_adjusted 0.4968 over 2 runs). Did not help: sample weighting, bit filtering, feature selection, LightGBM or CatBoost swaps, stacking, monotone constraints, count or FCFP kernels, multi-kernel sums, MACCS bits, target smoothing, blend-weight search (+0.0060), lipophilicity prior, and LightGBM regularization or tuning. MLP, SVR, kernel ridge and random Fourier features looked good on first runs (0.4879-0.4943) but their replicates were worse. Noise sd is about 0.0070, so gains under that are unreliable. Most of the 40-slot budget has been spent, with 6 aborts from not reading the file first. Next: read the current file first, tune GP noise and Morgan radius/size, and try a replicated MLP or RFF ensemble for diversity.
